additional_info.subject: RE: ID0452571-DC/Si-D/CH-[Y2/S5 313659082001] Charger out of service CRM:02698000590
additional_info.body:
Dear Alexander,
I am reaching out in regards of ticket
ID0452571.
I checked this morning the charger
JcsrWF
, and read the history of the past 2 onsite visits in the other tickets.
The charger this morning was presenting both outlets OoO. The issue had nothing to do with the routers, but it was the same issue mentioned in ticket
ID0449189
, i.e both EcoGs (and so both outlets) had a modbus related error:
I rebooted the charger form SCB this morning, and the outlets came back available since then. Since this issue already happened twice, we require further troubleshooting and support to identify the root cause of such behavior. I will escalate to R&D and EcoG the topic.
In the meanwhile, it has been proven that a reboot is an effective Workaround.
Therefore, if the issue appears again, please reboot the charger asap via SCB.
I will provide you feedback on the root-cause analysis as soon as available.

additional_info.subject: RE: AW: ID0452571-DC/Si-D/CH-[Y2/S5 313659082001] Charger out of service CRM:02698000590
additional_info.body:
Dear Alexander,
I am reaching out in regards of ticket
ID0452571.
The ticket was pending on feedback from R&D, in regards of unavailability of outlets with error "
Modbus maxdelay 5000 exceeded
".
From discussion with EcoG team, it was clarified that the error
correspond with a failure in the Modbus connection between the SECC and PLC. This could be due to a loose or faulty Ethernet cable.
Therefore, EcoG does not recognize the error as a bug or issue, but as a symptom/consequence of bad Modbus communication, hence a Hardware error. Reboot of the charger has been indicated as the way to restore the charger, in case this communication issue appears by time to time.
This correlates to the second onsite intervention that you mentioned in your last email, where the ETH cable was replaced. For what concerns the issues appeared in the first onsite activity, where a router was replaced and the CFast card was flashed, I can assure that it had nothing to do with the unavailability of outlets due to modbus communication that the charger experienced when this ticket was opened.
Since from EcoG and development I got feedback that it is a Hardware issue impacting the Modbus communication, from service side I can only recommend to keep the charger monitored and, in case of further Modbus communication issues appear, to verify the connection between EcoG and switch XF1.
Looking forward to hearing your feedback soon! Since no further action is pending on service side, as feedback from R&D has been provided, I would proceed to close this ticket once your feedback sis received.
With kind regards,
